label: copy-phase input u (fed-back u), from the 2nd copied token on
explanation: Fires when the model is fed back the letter u during the copy phase, i.e. the previously output original token was u, and only from the second copy-phase input onward (recall_idx >= 2). It is almost entirely silent on u in the original phase, on the delimiter, and on the first copy-phase input (recall_idx 1: a u there gives only weak or near-zero activation). It does not fire on any other input token, and it does not depend on what is output next or on the sequence length. Activations are fairly uniform (median ~4.1 of max 5.4). In the top examples, the second u of a consecutive uu run is somewhat weaker than the first.

issues: Claims verified. Test split: precision 1.000, recall 0.994, F1 0.997, mass recall 0.9998. There are no false positives on test.

Test misses are 430 steps holding about 0.0% of the activation mass. Almost all are u at recall_idx 1 with activation around 0.01-0.02 of max, which matches the stated near-silence there. There is also one stray s.

The profile matches the explanation. Original and delimiter phases show 0 activations. recall_idx 1 has 467 activations (0.1%). recall_idx 2 and up run at a flat ~3.3% rate. Other input tokens fire at most 3 times. Median 4.06, max 5.38.
The simpler predicate 'copy-phase input is u' scores dev F1 0.902 (precision 0.82), as claimed.

Minor nuance, not a refutation: magnitude varies somewhat with context. The second u of a uu run is weaker, and some early-copy u's are weaker (for example 0.40 at recall_idx 2). This is graded strength, not a change in when the feature fires.
